doc.title: Scott Jimmy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Little Willie John
summary: Willie John wanted to learn his ballads, and Scott describes his gangster-style short-man pose.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Also, before I forget, the other character that you hooked up with in the 1950s and the early 1960s, I guess, was Little Willie John, who – I always love Little Jimmy Scott and Little Willie John, and the two of you guys together.
We used to hang out together.
Oh you did? How did you meet?
He wanted me to teach him all my songs.
That’s what I was going to ask you. He wanted to be a balladeer.
Then I didn’t get around to doing that. I didn’t get around to doing that, and he sort of acted mad towards me, because I wouldn’t do it, but that’s Little Willie John, selfish.

Let me ask you something about that, because what I’ve always heard about Little Willie John – a lot of people think was one of the best rhythm-and-blues vocalists ever, along with Clyde McPhatter . . .
And there would have been Lubinsky’s bet for a hit . . .
If Herman . . .
. . . the kind of hit they wanted. Willie John would have been the thing.
That’s right.
But they never got around to . . .
He was over there in King Records with . . .
King Records, yeah.
. . . Sid Nathan.
And he’d never got around to dealing with Lubinsky.
Let me ask you this about you and your life – this is such a – whatever was heard about Little Willie John is that he had a short man’s complex.
Yeah.
That you couldn’t tell him nothing.
No, baby.
He’d take on the big . . .
Willie was a little short guy, and he wanted to be a gangster. His style was . . .
Gangster style.
. . . gangster style. He thought he could be a gangster. That’s what hurt him. He’d get around people, and they didn’t want to bother with it, because he didn’t know how to talk to people.
But in terms of you – do you ever feel like you had a short man’s complex?
Huh?
Do you feel like you ever had a short man’s complex the way Little Willie John did?
No, no. I never thought of that.
Back to mom. Accept it.

No, I never thought of myself being short or physically inadequate or whatever. But like I said, them guys, everybody wanted to be a big shot, and the kind of big shot they wanted to be was no good, because they wanted to be tough and bossy and run the show that they were involved in.
